kings2.15.p1.b1.text: In the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam’s reign over Israel, Azariah son of Amaziah became king of Judah. He was sixteen years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem fifty-two years. …

kings2.15.p1.b2.text: And he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, … Nevertheless, the high places were not taken away; the people continued sacrificing and burning incense there.

kings2.15.p1.b3.text: And the LORD afflicted the king with leprosy until the day he died, so that he lived in a separate house …

kings2.15.p1.b4.text: … while his son Jotham had charge of the palace and governed the people of the land.

kings2.15.p2.b1.text: In the thirty-eighth year of Azariah’s reign over Judah, Zechariah son of Jeroboam became king of Israel, and he reigned in Samaria six months.

kings2.15.p2.b2.text: Then Shallum son of Jabesh conspired against Zechariah, struck him down and killed him in front of the people, and reigned in his place.

kings2.15.p2.b3.text: So the word of the LORD spoken to Jehu was fulfilled: “Four generations of your sons will sit on the throne of Israel.”

kings2.15.p2.b4.text: … Shallum son of Jabesh became king, and he reigned in Samaria one full month. Then Menahem son of Gadi went up from Tirzah to Samaria, struck down and killed Shallum son of Jabesh, and reigned in his place.

kings2.15.p2.b5.text: At that time Menahem, starting from Tirzah, attacked Tiphsah and everyone in its vicinity, because they would not open their gates. …

kings2.15.p3.b1.text: In the thirty-ninth year of Azariah’s reign over Judah, Menahem son of Gadi became king of Israel, and he reigned in Samaria ten years.

kings2.15.p3.b2.text: Then Pul king of Assyria invaded the land, and Menahem gave Pul a thousand talents of silver in order to gain his support and strengthen his own grip on the kingdom.

kings2.15.p3.b3.text: Menahem exacted this money from each of the wealthy men of Israel—fifty shekels of silver from each man—to give to the king of Assyria. …

kings2.15.p3.b4.text: … So the king of Assyria withdrew and did not remain in the land.

kings2.15.p4.b1.text: In the fiftieth year of Azariah’s reign over Judah, Pekahiah son of Menahem became king of Israel and reigned in Samaria two years.

kings2.15.p4.b2.text: Then his officer, Pekah son of Remaliah, conspired against him along with Argob, Arieh, and fifty men of Gilead. And at the citadel of the king’s palace in Samaria, Pekah struck down and killed Pekahiah …

kings2.15.p4.b3.text: In the fifty-second year of Azariah’s reign over Judah, Pekah son of Remaliah became king of Israel, and he reigned in Samaria twenty years.

kings2.15.p4.b4.text: And he did evil in the sight of the LORD and did not turn away from the sins that Jeroboam son of Nebat had caused Israel to commit.

kings2.15.p5.b1.text: In the days of Pekah king of Israel, Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria came and captured Ijon, Abel-beth-maacah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor, Gilead, and Galilee, including all the land of Naphtali, and he took the people as captives to Assyria.

kings2.15.p5.b2.text: Then Hoshea son of Elah led a conspiracy against Pekah son of Remaliah. In the twentieth year of Jotham son of Uzziah, Hoshea attacked Pekah, killed him, and reigned in his place.

kings2.15.p6.b1.text: In the second year of the reign of Pekah son of Remaliah over Israel, Jotham son of Uzziah became king of Judah. He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem sixteen years. …

kings2.15.p6.b2.text: And he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, … Nevertheless, the high places were not taken away; the people continued sacrificing and burning incense there. Jotham rebuilt the Upper Gate of the house of the LORD.

kings2.15.p6.b3.text: (In those days the LORD began to send Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah against Judah.)

kings2.15.p6.b4.text: And Jotham rested with his fathers … And his son Ahaz reigned in his place.
